extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants/patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing and evaluating petitions to revive abandoned patent (including provisional and international) applications under 37 CFR 1.137, including timing, evidence, burden of proof, terminal disclaimer rules, and related procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt filing requirement for 37 CFR 1.137(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking to revive an “unavoidably” abandoned application must cause a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) to be filed without delay (i.e., promptly upon becoming notified, or otherwise becoming aware, of the abandonment of the application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden of continuing to present a grantable petition in a timely manner remains with the applicant until informed the petition is granted. Removal of the word “promptly” from the regulation does not permit delay; deliberate deferral in filing a petition will bar a finding that the entire delay was unavoidable (see Application of S).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of failing to file promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who fails to file a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) 'promptly' upon becoming notified, or otherwise becoming aware, of the abandonment will not be able to show that the entire delay from the due date for the reply until filing a grantable petition was unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delayed filing undermines ability to meet the 1.137(a) standard; deliberate deferral is specifically disfavored and may result in denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of 1.137(b) relief after 1.137(a) denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismissal or denial of a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) does not preclude obtaining relief under 37 CFR 1.137(b) on the basis of unintentional delay unless the decision indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 1.137(b) petition may be filed with the fee in 37 CFR 1.17(m), the required reply, a statement that the entire delay was unintentional, and any terminal disclaimer required by 37 CFR 1.137(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed petition forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/61 or PTO/SB/61PCT may be used to file a petition for revival of an unavoidably abandoned application (and corresponding PCT forms where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms PTO/SB/62 and PTO/SB/63 may be used when filing a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.137(d). Use of the prescribed forms helps ensure completeness and proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three periods of delay to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three periods to be considered during evaluation of a petition under 37 CFR 1.137: (A) the delay in reply that originally resulted in the abandonment; (B) the delay in filing an initial petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the application; and (C) the delay in filing a grantable petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation must account for each period separately and for the 'entire' delay from due date to filing of a grantable petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional abandonment or delay bars relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment considered a deliberately chosen course of action cannot be considered 'unintentional' within 37 CFR 1.137(b); deliberate choice not to seek or delay revival precludes finding of unavoidable or unintentional delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentional abandonment/delay is not excused by correctness of Office action, later discovery of new information, or competitor interest — examples include delaying revival until industry/competitor interest appears (antithesis of 'unavoidable' or 'unintentional'). See Maldague and Application of G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe-harbor timing thresholds (3 months and 1 year)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office generally will not question whether delay was intentional when a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 is filed (A) within 3 months of the date the applicant is first notified the application is abandoned, and (B) within 1 year of the date of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to file within 3 months of first notification to avoid the question of intentional delay being raised; filing within these periods is a practical way to avoid extensive scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to show 'unavoidable' or 'unintentional' if outside 3-month window
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) is not filed within 3 months of first notification, the Office will consider there to be a question whether the delay was unavoidable or unintentional and will require a showing of how the delay was 'unavoidable' (for (a)) or may require further information as to how the delay was 'unintentional' (for (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid delay in consideration of the merits, applicants should include a showing explaining how the delay was unavoidable or unintentional when filing after 3 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional information required if petition filed after 1 year
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) is not filed within 1 year of the date of abandonment, the Office will require (A) further information as to when the applicant or representative first became aware of the abandonment, and (B) a showing as to how the delay occurred despite the exercise of due care or diligence on the part of the applicant or representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should include the date they first became aware of the abandonment and a due-care/diligence showing to avoid processing delays or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for 1.137(a) and 1.137(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(a)(3) requires a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that the entire delay was unavoidable; 37 CFR 1.137(b)(3) requires a statement that the entire delay was unintentional and permits the Director to require additional information where there is a question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 1.137(a) the applicant must carry the burden of proof to establish the delay was unavoidable. For 1.137(b) ordinarily only a statement is required, but the Office may require the applicant to carry the burden of proof where there is doubt that the delay was unintentional (see Application of G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Whose delay is relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The question under 37 CFR 1.137 is whether the delay of the party having the right or authority to reply to avoid abandonment (or not reply) was unavoidable or unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant assigned entire right, title, and interest to a third party, the applicant's delay is irrelevant unless reassigned before the reply due date. If a third party controls prosecution (including partial assignee or licensee), that third party's decision binds the applicant unless the contract expressly limits the third party to fiduciary capacity (see Kim v. Quigg, Winkler, Futures Technology Ltd. v. Quigg).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement under 37 CFR 1.137(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(d) requires that a petition under either 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer (and fee) in specified application types and filing-date ranges (e.g., design applications; nonprovisional utility and plant applications filed before June 8, 1995; certain utility/plant applications filed June 8, 1995–May 29, 2000 that became abandoned during appeal, interference, or secrecy order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers dedicate part of the patent term equivalent to the period of abandonment (with date-dependent limits). The Office will not indicate the period disclaimed when granting revival. The filing of a terminal disclaimer does not substitute for showing unavoidable/unintentional delay, nor will a showing of unavoidable/unintentional delay waive the terminal disclaimer requirement. To seek waiver of the terminal disclaimer requirement, file a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 showing an 'extraordinary situation' where 'justice requires' relief (e.g., abandonment caused no actual delay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer exceptions and specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminal disclaimer requirement of 37 CFR 1.137(d) does not apply to (A) applications for which revival is sought solely for purposes of copendency with a utility/plant application filed on/after June 8, 1995; (B) lapsed patents; (C) reissue applications; or (D) reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995 the disclaimer period equals the lesser of the abandonment period or period extending beyond 20 years from filing (or earliest 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c) priority). For design applications the period equals the period of abandonment. Office cannot determine exact period at time of grant of revival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration timing under 37 CFR 1.137(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application or lapsed patent must be filed within 2 months of the decision refusing to revive or within such time set in the decision; unless indicated otherwise, this period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a renewed petition or request for reconsideration is filed outside the specified time, the Office may require a specific showing as to how the entire delay was 'unavoidable' (1.137(a)) or 'unintentional' (1.137(b)). Intentional delay due to deliberate choice remains immaterially unaffected by later changes in circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application revival limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application shall be regarded as abandoned 12 months after its filing date and shall not be subject to revival after such 12-month period. 37 CFR 1.137 allows revival of a provisional application abandoned for failure to reply, but a provisional will not be regarded as pending after twelve months from its filing date under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional may be revived to reestablish pendency only up to the original 12-month period; the petition must be accompanied by any outstanding reply (since continuing application in lieu of the reply is permitted only for nonprovisional applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's statement on petitions to set aside abandonment (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.181 states the examiner 'may be directed by the Director to furnish a written statement within a specific time setting forth the reasons for his or her decision upon the matters averred in the petition, supplying a copy thereof to the petitioner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless requested, however, such a statement should not be prepared. See MPEP §1002.01 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to abandoned applications (IFW and unpublished)
rubrics_metrics.description: Access will be provided to the application file for any non-Image File Wrapper (IFW) abandoned published application; for abandoned unpublished applications, access may be provided if the abandoned application is identified or relied upon in a U.S. patent application publication or patent, statutory invention registration, or an international application published under PCT Article 21(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When IFW access is unavailable electronically, copies can be ordered from the Office of Public Records with payment of fees per 37 CFR 1.19(b). A copy of the application-as-filed or specific document may be provided upon written request and fee. Form PTO/SB/68 may be used to request access under 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulling and forwarding abandoned application files
rubrics_metrics.description: Files of abandoned applications are pulled and forwarded to the Files Repository on a biweekly basis 1 month after the full 6-month statutory period has expired. Date of abandonment is after midnight of the date the shortened statutory period (including any extensions) expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate examiner should carefully scrutinize files to verify they are actually abandoned and check Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences files for allowed claims to avoid erroneous forwarding. The files are not pulled until the maximum permissible extension period plus one month has expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering patented and abandoned files (PALM process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patented and abandoned files are ordered via a PALM video display transaction; examiner inputs PALM location code, employee number, and patent/application numbers, and receives status: accepted, accepted but stored off-site, not accepted (file not at repository), not accepted (previous request pending), or not accepted (invalid number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files found are stapled to printed request and delivered; for IFW stored applications this ordering process is unnecessary. Drawings are delivered with file to avoid separation unless stored electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of abandonment and correspondence address responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Examining Corps mails a Notice of Abandonment form PTOL-1432 to the correspondence address of record for all applications that become abandoned for failure to prosecute, but mere failure to receive the notice does not affect the status of an abandoned application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must promptly file papers notifying the Office of any change of address in each application where the correspondence address is to be changed (see MPEP §402 and §601.03). Lack of diligent action after notice of abandonment may foreclose relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications are treated as publications and prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications are publications and are cited as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(b) effective from their date of publication in the Official Gazette. A defensive publication is prior art only as of its publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These printed publications may be used alone or in combination with other prior art in rejecting claims under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103. An application or portion from which such a publication was prepared may be used as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) only for evidence of prior knowledge of another. See MPEP §2136 and Ex parte Osmond.
